brief:
The International Court of Justice ruled Myanmar guilty of committing genocide, making it the first country ever convicted of the crime under the genocide convention, The Guardian reported. Judges issued a decision hailed as "a rare moment of justice" that establishes a roadmap for assessing intent in genocide cases.

The verdict has drawn attention beyond Myanmar, with observers noting its implications for other situations under international scrutiny. Legal analysts said the judgment carries messages relevant to ongoing cases elsewhere, particularly regarding how courts evaluate evidence of genocidal intent.

title: ICJ finds Myanmar guilty of genocide in historic ruling
